title: The Roman army and expansion

match.reason: The bank card covers the trained legions and Rome's expansion but says nothing about roads, forts or Roman law holding the empire together, which the new point teaches, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: The Roman army and expansion
card: Rome's army was made up of legions. A legion was a unit of several thousand soldiers, mostly citizens who were paid, trained and drilled to fight in disciplined groups.
Over many centuries the legions conquered lands around the Mediterranean Sea. They took territory in places such as Gaul, Spain, Greece, Egypt and North Africa.
Conquest was only the first step. Roman soldiers built roads and forts across new lands, so troops, messages and traders could travel quickly and rebellions could be met.
Roman law also spread to conquered peoples. A shared set of rules helped Rome govern distant provinces and hold the empire together.
draft.remember: Trained legions won the land. Roads, forts and Roman law helped Rome keep it.

a.q: Why were the roads that Roman soldiers built useful to Rome's rulers?
opts: They let troops and messages move quickly across the empire
They stopped conquered peoples from using Roman law
They were only built so traders could avoid Roman forts
They replaced the need for any soldiers in the provinces
a.why: Good roads let Rome send troops to trouble spots and carry messages across a large empire. The roads did not replace soldiers: legions and forts were still needed to hold the provinces.
a.clue: Think about how far away the edges of the empire were.

b.q: Rome's legions defeat a tribe in a distant region. Which action would best help Rome keep control of that region for the long term?
opts: Building a fort and a road, and applying Roman law
Withdrawing the legions straight after the victory
Leaving the tribe with no rules or laws to follow
Asking the tribe to build its own army to defend itself
b.why: Forts and roads let Rome station troops and respond quickly, while Roman law gave a shared set of rules for governing. Winning a battle alone does not hold land if the army leaves and no system is put in place.
b.clue: Winning the fight was only the first step.

wants.brief: A map of the Roman Empire at its height, showing the Mediterranean Sea, the provinces of Gaul, Spain, Greece, Egypt and North Africa, and the main Roman roads.
wants.why: It shows how far the legions' conquests reached and how roads linked the lands.

a.best: They let troops and messages move quickly across the empire

b.best: Building a fort and a road, and applying Roman law
